owner_question: Can news happening in the world -- big or niche -- identify stocks that are about to rise?

data.source: GDELT 1.0 Global Knowledge Graph daily files, https://data.gdeltproject.org/gkg/YYYYMMDD.gkg.csv.zip, free
data.sampling: one file per week, the Wednesday, 2013-04-03 onward. Every file is downloaded, reduced to (organisation, articles, article-weighted tone) and deleted; raw files are not kept. A Wednesday sample is 1/7 of daily coverage, which is ample for any company mentioned more than a handful of times a week and thin for small ones -- a density check is therefore the first gate.
data.fields_used: NUMARTS (articles), ORGANIZATIONS, TONE (first value: average tone)

identity_join.rule: GDELT organisation strings are lower-case names. An issuer is matched when its SEC filer name, normalised (case, punctuation, legal suffixes inc/corp/co/ltd/plc/holdings/group removed), equals a GDELT organisation string exactly. No fuzzy matching.
identity_join.gate: at least 300 liquid issuers (price >= $5, $5M median daily dollar volume) matched AND matched issuers with >= 1 mention per sampled week in at least half the weeks number >= 150. Below that the test is declared unreadable, not negative.
identity_join.known_weakness: common-word names (e.g. 'target', 'apple') collide with non-company mentions; the tone and growth signals are partly robust to this because they are changes, not levels.

point_in_time: a Wednesday file is usable from the following Friday close; the forward window starts at the first weekly close after that

signals.N1_attention_surge: log(mean articles over the last 4 sampled weeks + 1) - log(mean over the prior 26 sampled weeks + 1)
signals.N2_tone_shift: article-weighted tone over the last 4 sampled weeks minus over the prior 26
signals.declared_sign: POSITIVE for both: rising coverage and improving tone predict higher returns

measurement.measures: rank IC, decile spread, monotonicity (the Step 339-calibrated bar), block bootstrap
